continuity.arc_goal: Add complete linked workflow support to the Rust SDK: design user-facing API, implement protocol backing with compile-time validation, pass all tests, and prepare for integration against Restate server

progress_update.summary: We designed and implemented the full on_completion API for linked workflows, including compile-time handler signature validation via AsyncFn bounds (Rust 1.85+), runtime handler name resolution via type_name + macro-generated resolvers, and the ObjectContextT typed context path for same-object enforcement. We iterated through several design approaches before landing on the final architecture. Code review identified the Result<T, TerminalError> serde as a placeholder needing server protocol finalization.
progress_update.goal: Add linked workflow support to the Rust SDK with TDD approach. Success: start_linked(), unlink(), and on_completion() work on workflow clients, backed by CreateLinkCommand/RemoveLinkCommand protocol messages, with compile-time handler validation.
accomplished: Implemented on_completion() with AsyncFn-based CompletionHandlerFnT trait for compile-time handler signature and Res type validation
Added ObjectContextT<'ctx, S> typed context with #[restate_sdk::object(ObjectContextT)] macro attribute for same-object enforcement
Added RunRequestT, WorkflowClientT, RunT types to thread parent type S from context through to on_completion
Added LinkedRunRequest type that restricts terminal to start_linked() only after on_completion()
Fixed sys_link completion_handler_name arg, ingress Deserialize bound, rustfmt issues
Added Result<T, TerminalError> serde impls for completion handler input type
Added 5 trybuild negative compile tests (wrong Res, non-handler, wrong object, start_linked on service, unlink on service)
Removed default-path on_completion from RunRequest — now only available via typed ObjectContextT path
Ran comprehensive code review, addressed H1 (runtime panic) by removing default path
progress_update.now: Session ended after completing code review action items. All tests passing, all commits clean.
next_steps: Resolve Result<T, TerminalError> serde semantics once server protocol for completion handler invocation is finalized (C1/C2 from review)
Add integration test exercising linked workflows against a Restate container (requires server with linked-workflow support)
Consider squashing/cleaning commit history before PR
Update task_context.md with final API design decisions
constraints: shared-core on local path dependency (../sdk-shared-core) on linked-workflows branch
std::any::type_name format is not contractually stable — accepted risk
Server-side linked-workflows has known bugs (VO parent wrong InvocationId, cancel not propagating)
No MockVM in codebase — tests are either compile-time or full integration with real Restate
decisions: on_completion only available via ObjectContextT typed path — eliminated runtime panic risk from default path
Handler input type is Result<T, TerminalError> — maps to protocol success/failure, serde is placeholder until server protocol finalized
T-suffix naming convention: ObjectContextT, RunRequestT, WorkflowClientT, RunT, CompletionHandlerFnT
API: run_linked(req) on workflow client returns Request with linked:bool=true, .send() emits both OneWayCallCommand + CreateLinkCommand
API: unlink() on workflow client, fire-and-forget, emits RemoveLinkCommand
API: .send() returns impl InvocationHandle regardless of linked flag — CreateLink completion handled internally
open_questions: How does Restate server encode completion handler arguments? (success bytes vs failure bytes envelope)
Should we squash the many iterative commits before PR?
risks: Result<T, TerminalError> Deserialize always produces Ok(T) — cannot represent child failure until protocol is clarified
Server-side linked-workflows has critical bugs that may affect integration testing
